title.narrative: DRA - Sudan Joint Response 4

description.narrative: In partnership with Plan International, SOS Children village and 6 national partners, ZOA Sudan is implementing the Sudan Joint Response 4 for 2022 – 2023 funded by the Dutch Relief Alliance. The Sudan Joint Response 4 aims to address the needs in 2022 and 2023 by providing affected people with multi-sectoral assistance to respond to the immediate needs and protection risks of the most at risk and conflict affected people in targeted areas in Khartoum, North- Darfur, East Darfur, South Kordofan, White Nile and Gedaref, through an effective and efficient humanitarian response by Dutch NGOs, national partners and actors.ZOA Sudan is targeting five localities in Gedaref, North and South Darfur implementing FSL, WASH and Education interventions.

The SDNJR4 will align its program with the 2021 HRP Strategic Outcomes (1-3) as well as the Sudan COVID-19 Country Preparedness and Response Plan (4). The objectives will be adjusted when the 2022/2023 HRP will become available.1. Provide timely multi-sectoral life-saving assistance to crisis affected people to reduce mortality and morbidity.2. Improve vulnerable people’s access to livelihoods and life-sustaining basic services.3. Mitigate protection risks and respond to protection needs through humanitarian action.4. Prevent and contain the spread of COVID-19 and minimize mortality and morbidity.Complementary multi-sector assistance, resilience building and protection mainstreaming will remain at the core of the SDNJR4 programming as has been the case during Sudan Joint Response 1-3.The overall objective on the SDNJR4 is formulated as following: The Sudan Joint Response 4 aims to address the needs in 2022 and 2023 by providing affected people with multi-sectoral assistance to respond to the immediate needs and protection risks of the most at risk and conflict affected people in targeted areas in North-Darfur, South Darfur and Gedaref.

The primary target groups of the project are displaced communities in and out of camps, returnees, and host communities in North Darfur, South Darfur and Gedaref. The program participants include children, adolescents, youth, men, and women from households below the poverty line or households that included persons with disabilities (PWD).

In addition to the beneficiaries for 2022, 600 HHs received half-ration food vouchers, 12 farmer field schools sessions held targeting 325 farmers, seeds and tools distributed to 240 farmers and 2 seed bank committees with 10 persons as members. In East Darfur, 100HH received cash for food. Additionally, in Gedaref 98 farmers were supported and trained to produce agricultural products and 100 manuals were distributed. Also, 150 PWD received in-kind food support.

comment.narrative: ZOA expects that the programme will be adapted at least twice due to community's feedback.

The project had been majorly modified 3 times in total to be exact. The first was to incorporate the changes required to accommodate the top up funds. The second round was during the reprogramming where activities and budgets were shifted from South Darfur to Gedaref and East Darfur. The last round was to move activities from North Darfur to Gedaref.
